chapters.title: La salle de classe
chapters.description: Master classroom objects, instructions, articles, possession with 'de', the essential verbs avoir & être, and prepositions of place.

lessons.title: Classroom Objects & People
lessons.description: Build typing muscle memory for everyday classroom nouns and masculine/feminine articles (le, la, l').

items.hint: Notice the grave accent on è in règle.
Circumflex accent on ê in fenêtre.
Two acute accents: é in télé-.
Cedilla ç gives a soft 's' sound before 'o'.

lessons.title: Classroom Instructions & Questions
lessons.description: Type real sentences a French teacher uses in class — commands, dates, and asking what things are.

items.en: What is this? / What is it?
items.hint: Literally 'What is it that it is?' (p. 10).
Answers to 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' usually start with C'est.
Plural/polite command to the whole class.
Circumflex accent on ê in fenêtre.
Ends in -ez for the whole class.
Ends in -ez for the whole class.

items.fr: Georges, ferme la porte, s'il te plaît!
items.hint: Singular informal uses 'ferme' and 's'il te plaît'.
Everyday French way to ask the day (p. 11).
Days of the week aren't capitalized in French.
Use 'il' for 'it' when referring to a masculine noun (cahier).

lessons.title: Articles, Possessives & 'De'
lessons.description: Practice 'the', 'a/some', 'my', 'your' across genders and plurals, plus showing possession with de, d', du, de la, des.

items.hint: 'tes' is used for all plural nouns.
Use 'mon/ton' even for feminine nouns starting with a vowel (p. 13).
Don't forget the cedilla in garçons.
Literally 'the pencil case of Sophie' — no apostrophe-s in French!
'de' shortens to d' before a vowel.

lessons.title: Verb Avoir (To Have) & Age
lessons.description: Type every form of avoir (j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont) and talk about age.

items.hint: Third-person singular of avoir is 'a' (no accent!).

items.en: They (m.) have a computer in the classroom.
items.fr: Ils ont un ordinateur dans la classe.
Marc a les stylos de Jean.
items.hint: Names take the same verb form as il/elle: 'a'.
Literally 'What age have you?' — circumflex on â in âge (p. 21).
French uses avoir ('I have eleven years'), not être.

items.en: What do you have in your pencil case?
items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu as dans ta trousse?

items.en: In my classroom, there is a pen and some pencils.
items.fr: Dans ma salle de classe, il y a un stylo et des crayons.

lessons.title: Verb Être (To Be) & Where Things Are
lessons.frenchTitle: Le verbe être et les prépositions
lessons.description: Master all forms of être (je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont) and say where objects are located.

items.en: We are also in the class.
items.fr: Nous sommes aussi dans la classe.

items.en: Are you (pl.) also in my class?
items.fr: Vous êtes aussi dans ma classe?
items.hint: Circumflex accent on ê in êtes.

items.en: The girls are in the class.
items.fr: Les filles sont dans la classe.
Le stylo de Pierre est rouge.

items.en: Sophie's ruler is in Anne-Marie's pencil case.
items.fr: La règle de Sophie est dans la trousse d'Anne-Marie.
items.hint: Exercice 2.14 (p. 20) — combines être, dans, and d'.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 Mastery Challenge
lessons.description: Test everything from Chapter 2 in one fast-paced typing sprint — nouns, commands, avoir, être, and full sentences.

items.en: I have five pencils and two pens.
items.fr: J'ai cinq crayons et deux stylos.

items.en: I am Nicolas and I am eleven years old.
items.fr: Je suis Nicolas et j'ai onze ans.
items.hint: Exercice 2.17 (p. 22) — être for name, avoir for age!

items.en: The pupils in the classroom have books.
items.fr: Les élèves dans la salle de classe ont des livres.

items.en: The boy in the classroom is called Pierre.
items.fr: Le garçon dans la salle de classe s'appelle Pierre.

items.en: Philippe is a friend of Charles.
items.fr: Philippe est un ami de Charles.

chapters.title: Chez nous
chapters.description: Describe your home and a French breakfast, master first-group (-ER) verbs, mon/ton/son, voici/voilà, and 'n'est-ce pas?'.

lessons.title: Home & French Breakfast
lessons.description: Learn French breakfast foods, tableware, and morning conversation from Georges and Martine's story.

items.hint: Hyphenated with an acute accent on é.

items.en: a slice of bread with butter/jam
No, Mum, I'm coming right away!
items.fr: Non, maman, j'arrive tout de suite!

lessons.title: First-Group (-ER) Verbs
lessons.description: Type the universal -ER verb endings (-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent) and combine aimer/adorer with infinitives.

items.hint: One French present form covers both 'eats' and 'is eating'.

items.en: Dad is looking at the newspaper.
Georges is eating a tartine with his tea.
items.fr: Georges mange une tartine avec son thé.

items.en: She gives a slice of bread to Robert.
items.fr: Elle donne une tartine à Robert.

items.en: Are you listening to the radio?
No, we are listening to music.
items.fr: Non, nous écoutons de la musique.

items.hint: Use the full -er infinitive after aimer/adorer (p. 28).

items.en: Nicolas and Robert love to eat!

lessons.title: House Rooms, Mon/Ton/Son & Voici/Voilà
lessons.description: Tour a French home, distinguish his/her with son/sa/ses, use voici/voilà/il y a, and wrap up with n'est-ce pas?

items.en: Martine is looking for her pen.
items.hint: Use 'son' for 'her' here because 'stylo' is masculine!
'son/sa/ses' agrees with the noun, not the owner (p. 29).

items.en: There is a dog in the house.
items.fr: Il y a un chien dans la maison.
items.hint: Use 'il y a' when simply giving information (p. 30).

lessons.title: Chapter 3 Exam-Style Challenge
lessons.description: Type complete exam-style sentences from Exercices 3.12 & 3.13 — combining verbs, numbers, possession, and rooms.

items.fr: Martine arrive et mange le petit-déjeuner.

items.en: In the house, there is a dog and a cat.
items.fr: Dans la maison, il y a un chien et un chat.

items.en: Here is a photo of my parents.
items.fr: Voici une photo de mes parents.

items.en: Sophie's exercise book is on the table.
items.fr: Le cahier de Sophie est sur la table.

items.en: There are three books and twelve pencils on my table.
items.fr: Il y a trois livres et douze crayons sur ma table.

items.en: Mum and Charles arrive in the dining room.
items.fr: Maman et Charles arrivent dans la salle à manger.
Sophie est dans la salle de bains.

items.en: Paul and Georges are watching television.
items.fr: Paul et Georges regardent la télévision.

items.en: Marie-Claire, are you listening to the radio?
Martine likes croissants; they are delicious!
items.fr: Martine aime les croissants; ils sont délicieux!
items.hint: From the breakfast story on p. 24.

items.en: There is a book in her bag.
items.fr: Il y a un livre dans son sac.

chapters.title: La vie quotidienne et l'heure
chapters.description: Master reflexive verbs (se réveiller, se lever, se laver, s'habiller), telling the time, faire & mettre, home chores, and negatives (ne...pas).

lessons.title: Reflexive Verbs & Morning Routine
lessons.description: Practice daily 'self' verbs (se réveiller, se lever, se laver, s'habiller) and follow Georges and Martine's morning routine.

items.hint: Reflexive verbs start with 'se' or s' (p. 34).
Takes a grave accent è in je me lève / elle se lève.

items.en: I wash / I am washing myself.
Georges wakes up at seven o'clock.
items.fr: Georges se réveille à sept heures.

items.en: Martine gets up at quarter past seven.
items.fr: Martine se lève à sept heures et quart.

items.en: Martine gets dressed at seven twenty.
items.fr: Martine s'habille à sept heures vingt.

items.en: Georges washes at half past seven.
items.fr: Georges se lave à sept heures et demie.

items.en: Martine and Georges come downstairs at quarter to eight.
items.fr: Martine et Georges descendent à huit heures moins le quart.

items.en: It is eight o'clock. It's breakfast time.
items.fr: Il est huit heures. C'est l'heure du petit-déjeuner.

items.en: She gets up in her bedroom.
items.fr: Elle se lève dans sa chambre.
Nous nous habillons avant le petit-déjeuner.

lessons.title: Telling the Time & Numbers 13–30
lessons.description: Ask and tell the time (o'clock, quarter past, half past, quarter to, noon, midnight) and type numbers 13 to 30.

items.hint: Standard way to ask the time (p. 35).

items.fr: Il est dix heures et demie.
Il est deux heures et quart.
Il est quatre heures moins le quart.

items.en: It is three o'clock in the afternoon.
items.fr: Il est trois heures de l'après-midi.
items.hint: du matin / de l'après-midi / du soir (p. 36).

items.fr: Ah non! Je suis en retard!

items.en: Usually, I get up at seven o'clock.
items.fr: D'habitude, je me lève à sept heures.

lessons.title: Faire, Mettre & Helping at Home
lessons.description: Use faire (to do/make) and mettre (to put/lay) to talk about housework, sports, hobbies, and how often you help at home.

items.en: I do my homework at seven p.m.
items.fr: Je fais mes devoirs à sept heures du soir.

items.en: Dad does the washing-up after breakfast.
items.fr: Papa fait la vaisselle après le petit-déjeuner.

items.en: You (pl.) go skiing in the Alps.
items.fr: Vous faites du ski dans les Alpes.

lessons.title: The Negative (ne ... pas)
lessons.description: Wrap ne ... pas (or n' ... pas before a vowel) around any French verb to say what doesn't happen.

items.hint: Place 'ne' before the verb and 'pas' after it (p. 43).
'ne' shortens to n' before a vowel or silent 'h' (p. 43).

items.en: Marie-Yvonne does not eat a lot.
Patrick does not do his homework.
items.fr: Patrick ne fait pas ses devoirs.

items.en: Linda does not do the washing-up.
items.fr: Linda ne fait pas la vaisselle.

items.fr: Je ne sors pas les poubelles.

items.fr: D'habitude, je ne fais pas mes devoirs à l'école.

items.en: My father does not watch TV in the evening.

chapters.title: On va à l'école!
chapters.description: Learn the verb aller, transport, days of the week, school subjects, opinions, colours, and masculine/feminine adjectives.

lessons.title: Verb Aller & Transport
lessons.description: Say how you travel to school and around town using aller with en (enclosed vehicles) and à (bike, foot, motorbike).

items.hint: Use 'à' for bike and on foot (p. 46).

items.en: Do you go to school by car?
items.fr: Tu vas à l'école en voiture?

items.en: No, I go to school by train. I live far away.
items.fr: Non, je vais à l'école en train. J'habite loin.

items.en: Nicolas goes to school by taxi.
items.fr: Nicolas va à l'école en taxi.

items.en: We are going to Paris by train.
items.fr: Nous allons à Paris en train.

items.en: You (pl.) go to school by bike.
items.fr: Vous allez à l'école à vélo.

lessons.title: Days of the Week & School Subjects

lessons.title: Adjectives, Colours & Agreement
lessons.description: Describe people and objects with colours (placed after the noun) and master regular & irregular feminine adjective endings.

items.hint: Adjectives normally come AFTER the noun in French (p. 52).

items.en: The house is white and black.
items.fr: La maison est blanche et noire.

items.en: Paul is tall. Marie is small.
items.fr: Paul est grand. Marie est petite.
items.hint: Add -e to make regular adjectives feminine (p. 52).
Adjectives ending in -e stay the same in feminine (p. 51).
Adjectives ending in -x change to -se in feminine (p. 55–56).

items.en: My pencil case is brand new.
items.hint: Adjectives ending in -f change to -ve: neuf → neuve (p. 55–56).

items.en: My father is handsome and my mother is beautiful.
items.fr: Mon père est beau et ma mère est belle.

items.hint: nouveau / nouvelle (nouvel before a vowel, p. 56).

chapters.title: La date, les nombres, les prix
chapters.description: Type months, birthdays, numbers up to 1000, market shopping with acheter, il faut, vouloir, and pouvoir.

lessons.title: Months, Birthdays & Numbers 40–1000
lessons.frenchTitle: Les mois et les grands nombres
lessons.description: Master all 12 French months, say when your birthday is, and type French numbers from 40 to 1000.

items.en: My birthday is the first of January.
items.fr: Mon anniversaire est le premier janvier.
items.hint: Use 'le premier' only for the 1st of a month (p. 57).
'il faut + infinitive' = it is necessary / must (p. 58).

lessons.title: Shopping, Acheter, Vouloir & Pouvoir
lessons.frenchTitle: Au marché: acheter, vouloir et pouvoir
lessons.description: Ask market prices, conjugate acheter (with its grave accent è), and practice vouloir (to want) and pouvoir (can).

items.en: How much is a kilo of bananas?
items.fr: Un kilo de bananes, c'est combien?

items.fr: Un euro dix, s'il vous plaît.

items.fr: Nous achetons deux kilos de carottes.

items.fr: J'achète des pommes de terre et un melon.

items.fr: Ils achètent des tomates et des pommes.

items.en: Where there is a will, there is a way!
Yes, please / I would like that.
Do you want to watch TV?
We want to eat right away.

items.en: I want to do my homework.
She cannot, because she has no money.
items.fr: Elle ne peut pas, parce qu'elle n'a pas d'argent.

items.en: Philippe wants to buy a birthday card for his mum.
items.fr: Philippe veut acheter une carte d'anniversaire pour sa maman.
items.hint: From the shopping story on p. 64.

items.en: I can go to school by train.
items.fr: Je peux aller à l'école en train.

items.en: You (pl.) can stay here if you want.
items.fr: Vous pouvez rester ici si vous voulez.

grammarGuides.title: The, A/Some, My, Your, His/Her
grammarGuides.summary: Articles and possessives agree with the gender and number of the noun they describe. Before a vowel or silent 'h', le/la become l', and ma/ta/sa become mon/ton/son.

grammarGuides.title: Showing Possession with 'de'
grammarGuides.summary: French never uses 's. Instead, flip the phrase to 'the X of Y': Sophie's pencil case → la trousse de Sophie.

grammarGuides.title: Essential Verbs: Avoir & Être
grammarGuides.summary: Avoir (to have) is also used for age (J'ai onze ans). Être (to be) describes who, what, or where people and things are.

grammarGuides.title: First-Group (-ER) Verbs
grammarGuides.summary: Remove -er from the infinitive (e.g. regarder → regard-) and add the ending. One French form translates both 'I watch' and 'I am watching'.

grammarGuides.title: Reflexive Verbs & Telling the Time
grammarGuides.summary: Reflexive verbs pair each subject with a matching 'self' pronoun (me, te, se, nous, vous, se). Use 'il est ... heures' for time, plus et quart, et demie, and moins le quart.
rows: Il est deux heures et quart.
Il est dix heures et demie.
Il est quatre heures moins le quart.
du matin / de l'après-midi / du soir

grammarGuides.title: Negatives (ne...pas) & Adjective Agreement
grammarGuides.summary: Make any verb negative with ne (n' before a vowel) ... pas. Adjectives normally follow the noun and agree in gender (often adding -e, or special patterns below).
rows: Il ne mange pas / Il n'écoute pas

grammarGuides.title: Numbers (40–1000), Acheter & Il faut
grammarGuides.summary: Months and days are lowercase in French. Use 'le premier' for the 1st of the month. 'Acheter' takes a grave accent (è) everywhere except nous/vous. 'Il faut + infinitive' means 'must / ought to'.
